title: Delilah (Judges 16:4–21)
hook: strength given away a secret at a time

segments.voice: Yesterday, Samson's mother, never named, visited by the angel twice. Your line was the angel came to her. Today, her son is grown, and he falls in love.

In the valley of Sorek lives a woman named Delilah, and the lords of the Philistines come to her with an offer. Find out where Samson's great strength lies, and each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver. The text says Samson loved her. It never says she loved him. And she doesn't hide what she's doing. She asks him straight out: tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and how you could be bound.
screen: `SILVER FROM THE PHILISTINE LORDS.` → `SAMSON LOVED HER.` → `TELL ME WHERE YOUR STRENGTH LIES.`

segments.voice: He lies. Bind me with fresh bowstrings, and I'll be weak. She does, with men lying in wait in the room, and cries: the Philistines are upon you, Samson. He snaps them like thread. Again: new ropes, never used. He snaps those too. The third time, listen. Weave the locks of my hair into the loom. Still a lie, but drifting toward the truth: now it's about his hair. Then she presses him: "How canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me?" She pressed him daily, the text says, until his soul was vexed unto death. And he tells her everything. No razor has come on my head; I've been a Nazirite to God from my mother's womb. Some readers hear the strength living not in the hair itself, but in the vow his mother was given, with the hair as its sign. She lulls him to sleep on her knees and calls a man to shave him. When she cries, the Philistines are upon you, he wakes and thinks, I'll go out as at other times and shake myself free. Then the line that hurts: he did not know that the Lord had departed from him. Nobody took his strength in one blow. He handed it over a little at a time, each lie a step closer to the truth.
screen: `BOWSTRINGS, THEN NEW ROPES.` · `THE THIRD LIE IS ABOUT HIS HAIR.` · `HOW CANST THOU SAY, I LOVE THEE?` · `HE DID NOT KNOW THE LORD HAD GONE.`

segments.voice: Name one thing that holds you up, sleep, a friendship, a daily prayer, staying sober, a promise you keep, and look honestly for the small ways you've been giving it away, because someone asked or because saying no was tiring. Don't scold yourself; just see it, and choose one small way to guard it.
Delilah. The woman of the valley of Sorek who asked again and again where Samson's strength lay, until he told her.
Your line: guard your strength. Even Samson didn't notice it slipping away. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jews read the Samson and Delilah chapters as part of the Former Prophets, and rabbinic commentary links Samson's strength to his Nazirite vow and asks why he gave his secret away.

chat.meaning: Three lies drifted toward the truth; pressed daily, he told her he was a Nazirite, and she had a man shave him while he slept.

Delilah.meaning: the woman who pressed Samson for the secret of his strength

Nazirite.meaning: one set apart to God from birth; no razor on the head

Philistines.meaning: Samson's enemies, whose lords paid Delilah

notes: Audit: closing line no longer says he gave his strength away 'a secret at a time' (he tells three lies and one secret, 16:17); it now follows the lies drifting toward the truth, as the teach shows.
Judges 16:15 quoted from the KJV; JPS 1917 wording not verified.
'Eleven hundred pieces of silver' from each lord is stated in 16:5.
The KJV's 'seven green withs' (16:7) is rendered 'fresh bowstrings' (a common reading of the Hebrew yetarim lachim); the number seven is left out. A Keeper may prefer 'fresh cords'.
'Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth' (16:6) is spoken unquoted in the hook; it matches the KJV.
'Then the line that hurts' replaces an earlier superlative.
Strength tied to the vow, not the hair itself: an interpretive reading supported by 16:17 and 13:5; Keeper to confirm the framing.
